data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides as seen in the close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear crowded at the terminal end of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided single blades)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (blades are widest near the middle and taper toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tips taper gradually to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly curved, not wedge-shaped or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single main midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, spaced closely and parallel to each other (prominent and creating a rugose surface texture)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): rugose (surface is uneven due to sunken secondary veins)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visible but relatively brief)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and rounded)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid, brown, and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): present (small, reddish, lanceolate stipules are clearly visible at the base of the petioles in the close-up images)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: New growth at the shoot tip exhibits a reddish coloration, contrasting with the mature green leaves. Some leaves show minor physical damage including holes and missing margins.
